sources.title: Position of the Council at first reading on the Payment Services Regulation (ST 8543/1/26 REV 1, 2023/0210(COD))
sources.notes: PDF text read 2026-11-14 (389 pages, dated Brussels, 2026-11-04, headed as adopted by the Council on 2026-10-29). Article 124: entry into force on the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal; most provisions apply 21 months after entry into force, Articles 51 and 58 after 27 months, and Articles 92 and 118 from entry into force. The recitals deem e-money tokens to be electronic money and say that transfer services for e-money tokens on behalf of clients could qualify as the payment service of executing payment transactions; recital 29 excludes trading and exchange of e-money tokens but not their transfer to pay for goods or services. Recitals relevant to agent payments: 158 (strong customer authentication applies when the initial merchant-initiated mandate is set up, not to each later merchant-initiated transaction), 162 (European Digital Identity Wallets as a means of authentication), 170 (operators of pass-through wallets need outsourcing agreements and the payer's PSP keeps full liability), 16 and 171 (technical service providers and payment schemes are liable for failing to support strong customer authentication, capped at the transaction amount). No provision addresses AI agents: 'artificial intelligence' appears once, in a fraud-monitoring recital, and 'agentic', 'AI agent' and 'autonomous' have no hits.

sources.title: Position of the Council at first reading on the Payment Services Directive (PSD3) (ST 8535/1/26 REV 1, 2023/0209(COD))
sources.notes: PDF text read 2026-11-14 (184 pages, dated Brussels, 2026-11-04, headed as adopted by the Council on 2026-10-29). Article 49: Member States transpose and apply the Directive 21 months after entry into force; Article 48 repeals PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366) and the second E-Money Directive (2009/110/EC) from the same date; Article 43 lets already authorized payment institutions continue until 27 months after entry into force. Article 47 inserts a new MiCA Article 60(4a): a payment institution may provide crypto-asset services in relation to e-money tokens for the purposes of its payment services, where they are equivalent to the payment services it is authorized for, if it notifies its home competent authority at least 40 working days before it starts. No provision addresses AI agents.

sources.title: Implementing the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act for the Issuance of Stablecoins by Entities Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (final rule, FR Doc. 2026-21706)
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and Department of the Treasury (Federal Register)
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-14 through the Federal Register API record and full text (2026-11-15T03:23Z UTC). Final rule at 91 FR 67000 to 67194 (195 pages), Docket OCC-2025-0372, RIN 1557-AF41, amending 12 CFR parts 3, 6, 8, 15 and 19; effective 2027-01-18. The preamble calls it the first final rule issued by a primary Federal payment stablecoin regulator implementing the Act and says 2027-01-18 will be the effective date of the Act. It covers permitted and foreign payment stablecoin issuers under the OCC's jurisdiction and certain custody activities; Bank Secrecy Act, AML and sanctions rules are left to a separate rulemaking with Treasury. No provision addresses AI agents: 'artificial intelligence' and 'agentic' have no hits, and the preamble declines technology-specific requirements for smart contracts or super intelligence. Companion information-collection notices (FR Doc. 2026-21704 and 2026-21705, 2026-10-23) and a correction (FR Doc. 2026-22036, 2026-10-29) were published separately. A Federal Register search on 2026-11-14 found no final rule from the FDIC, Federal Reserve, NCUA or Treasury implementing the Act. Re-checked 2026-11-21 (Federal Register API and public inspection): still the only final rule from a primary federal payment stablecoin regulator; the FDIC's issuer rule and FinCEN's issuer AML and sanctions rule were received for OIRA review on 2026-11-18 (src-policy-oira-eo12866-20261120).

sources.title: Super Intelligence: Supervisory Framework (OCC, attachment to News Release 2026-97)
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.notes: PDF text read 2026-11-14 (22 pages). Section 2.2: a highly autonomous payment agent may present greater risk than an agent used only for internal drafting. Section 3.1: a fully autonomous, customer-facing payment agent sits at Tier 1 (critical) regardless of how well it performs in testing, and the section 3.2 table lists 'Autonomous payment agent' under Tier 1. Section 2.10 treats customer, counterparty, fintech or agentic-commerce systems the bank does not control as a channel risk, with identity, provenance, delegation, authentication, monitoring, velocity limits, dispute handling, suspension and revocation calibrated to the action requested. Appendix A defines agentic SI. No search supports calling it the first federal supervisory document on agent payments.

sources.title: Using AI agents: complying with consumer law
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-14 through the GOV.UK content API (2026-11-15T03:46Z UTC). First published 2026-03-09; updated 2026-10-30 with the change note 'DRCF joint statement on agentic AI published.' The page says that on 2026-10-30 the members of the Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum (the CMA, FCA, ICO and Ofcom) published a joint statement on protecting people and businesses in an agentic AI economy, covering the work under way at each regulator, continued collaboration with government and how existing legal and regulatory frameworks apply to agents. The guidance says a business is responsible for what an AI agent does in the same way it is responsible for what an employee does, even if someone else designed or provides the agent, and applies the DMCC Act 2024, the Consumer Rights Act 2015 and the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 to agent search results, pricing and refunds. The joint statement itself (drcf.org.uk) answered HTTP 403 and was not read.

sources.notes: Read 2026-11-14 through the GOV.UK content API. CMA research first published 2026-03-09 and updated 2026-10-30 to point to the DRCF members' joint statement of that day.

sources.title: Stablecoin Regulations (proposed), Canada Gazette, Part I, Vol. 160, No. 43
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-14 (HTTP 200, 2026-11-15T03:41Z UTC). Prepublished 2026-10-24 under the Stablecoin Act and the Retail Payment Activities Act, with representations invited within 60 days of publication. The Regulatory Impact Analysis Statement says the proposed Regulations would come into force alongside the Stablecoin Act on a day or days fixed by order of the Governor in Council, with the intention of fall 2027. Issuer rules cover Bank of Canada registration, one-to-one reserves, redemption with capped fees, governance, risk, data security and recovery, and no yield. An amendment to the Retail Payment Activities Regulations treats a unit as meeting prescribed criteria if it is a stablecoin issued by an issuer on the Bank of Canada's list (or by a financial institution under substantially similar law), so payment service providers that perform payment functions with such stablecoins would have to register with the Bank of Canada and meet its safeguarding and operational-risk rules, while financial institutions that issue such stablecoins would not themselves be subject to the Retail Payment Activities Act. Proposed, not final. Canada Gazette Part II issues of 2026-10-07, 2026-10-21 and 2026-11-04 carry no commencement order for the Stablecoin Act.

sources.title: The EBA classifies USDC as the first significant e-money token in the European Union
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-14 (HTTP 200, 2026-11-15T03:59Z UTC). The EBA classified USDC, issued by Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS, as a significant e-money token under MiCA. From 2026-11-12 USDC is under the dual supervision MiCA sets for significant e-money tokens: the EBA supervises own funds, the reserve of assets, liquidity and recovery and redemption plans, while the French ACPR keeps governance, qualifying holdings, fit and proper, outsourcing and conflicts of interest.

sources.title: Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime (SAFR)
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200, 2026-11-21T07:42Z UTC); the page shows Published Date: 03 July 2026 and files the item under Monographs/Information Papers. MAS describes SAFR as a framework for the governance of AI agents in financial services: how agent actions are authorized, how human oversight is activated and what is recorded at the point of every decision, with implementation considerations for institutions that deploy it. It was developed jointly by the financial industry under MAS's BuildFin.ai initiative. The paper itself (PDF, 958.8 KB) was not read. An information paper, not a rule or guideline.

sources.title: Ministerial Keynote by Mr Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Trade), and Chairman of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, at the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 on 18 November 2026
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200, 2026-11-21T07:42Z UTC; earlier that morning the verifier's curl got an Akamai maintenance page and used WebFetch). Page dated 18 November 2026. Paragraph 10 announces three National AI Missions for Financial Services: strengthening financial crime prevention, improving access to financing and enabling safe agentic transactions. Paragraphs 27 to 32 (Enabling safe agentic transactions): agents must operate within defined authority and limits; institutions and enterprises remain accountable for actions taken on their behalf; MAS will work with industry to test practical solutions in controlled environments, one area being how AI agents can interact with purpose bound money (MAS's spelling) to transact within defined authority and limits; the trials are to examine common approaches to identity, authority, accountability and interoperability. Paragraph 33: the Future of Finance Institute (FFI) takes the missions forward. A statement of intent, not a rule or guideline. The speech does not mention the Agentic Money Sandbox or a know-your-agent protocol. The Singapore FinTech Festival ran from 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-20 (MAS media release of 2026-11-15).

sources.title: MAS and Future of Finance Institute Set Out Initiatives in Support of National AI Missions for Financial Services
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200; dateline Singapore, 18 November 2026). Paragraph 5: FFI will establish an Agentic Money Sandbox, a controlled environment for financial institutions to develop and test how AI agents can transact using digital money within defined authority, limits and safeguards; initial use cases will include agent-initiated payments and treasury management across participating financial institutions, so that controls are tested before such uses go live. Paragraph 8 unveils FFI's financial institution launch partners (DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB); the release does not name them as sandbox participants and gives no start date for the sandbox. FFI is described as a public-private collaboration established in Singapore. The release does not mention SAFR, a know-your-agent protocol, stablecoins or tokenized deposits.

sources.title: Advancing the Future of Finance: From Foundation to Scale (keynote address by Mr Chia Der Jiun, Managing Director, Monetary Authority of Singapore, at the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 on 19 November 2026)
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200, 2026-11-21T07:42Z UTC); Published Date: 19 November 2026. Paragraph 47: some users are giving agents their login credentials to financial accounts, and the Managing Director would not advise giving personal agents such access because there is insufficient assurance of safety (advice, not a prohibition). Paragraph 49 refers to the first phase of SAFR (src-policy-mas-safr). Paragraphs 51 to 53: in the new phase of SAFR, MAS will facilitate the development of a know your agent protocol for trusted information exchange between customer agents and financial institutions, covering who the agent is and whom it represents, what authority it has been given, what mandate it operates under and what assurance exists about its provenance and reliability; with this information institutions can establish a dedicated secure channel for agent access. Paragraphs 55 to 57 (Agentic Money Sandbox): MAS will also set up a sandbox with FFI for two use cases, corporate treasury management (banks use tokenized deposits for permitted treasury actions) and payments (banks and payment service providers let customer agents execute payment instructions with digital money such as tokenized deposits or stablecoins, after verifying the agent's identity and authority and applying risk controls). No timeline or participants are given for SAFR's new phase or the protocol; for the sandbox the speech names only FFI. It names no card network, no Ant International and none of the protocols on this site.

sources.title: Proposal for a Regulation on promoting fair business-to-consumer commercial practices in the offline and digital single market, and repealing Directive 2005/29/EC (Digital Fairness Act), COM(2026) 1100 final
sources.notes: Commission document page and its PDF read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200; PDF 512,328 bytes, text extracted locally). Cover: Brussels, 11.11.2026, COM(2026) 1100 final, procedure 2026/0356 (COD). The canonical text is on EUR-Lex (CELEX 52026PC1100, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52026PC1100), which answered HTTP 202 with an empty body to the first read on 2026-11-21; a later read the same day (HTTP 200, 418,361 bytes) showed the same Article 3(21) definition and the same Articles 26, 27 and 40, and Article 26(7) has the consumer's system send the consumer's contact details to the trader. A proposed regulation that would repeal the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive 2005/29/EC; companion proposals amend Directives 2011/83/EU and 2002/58/EC for simplification (COM(2026) 1110) and revise the CPC Regulation (COM(2026) 1120). Article 3(21) defines an automated system as software capable of carrying out actions and taking decisions producing legal effects for its user, including concluding contracts, without the need for human intervention. Article 26 (automated systems for contracting on behalf of a consumer with a trader) binds traders that make such systems available to consumers: tools to express choices and set and adjust the parameters at any time (26(1)); at first use the consumer must expressly choose to confirm all contracts, to confirm only a type of contracts based on criteria the consumer sets, including a maximum price and a time limit for that choice, or no confirmation (26(2)); the choice is confirmed on a durable medium (26(3)); where confirmation is chosen, at least the information of Article 6(1), points (a) to (e), (h) to (k), (o) and (p), of Directive 2011/83/EU (26(4)(a)); disclosure of any payment the trader receives for proposing a contract and of any conflict of interest, after which the consumer must confirm that contract whatever the earlier choice (26(4)(b)); the trader and the provider of the system may identify and authenticate themselves with a European Business Wallet or a European Digital Identity Wallet (26(5)), and European Business Wallets may also identify the system and establish on whose behalf it acts (26(6)); the consumer's system transmits the contact details needed for performance (26(7)); the trader confirms the contract on a durable medium (26(8)); traders must not design interfaces that require consumers to use automated systems (26(9)); Article 26 does not apply to the provision of financial services (26(10)). Article 27: where both sides contract solely through automated systems, the trader may give the Article 6(1) information only in a commonly used machine-readable format, is exempt from Article 6a, and Articles 8(1) to (4) and (8) of Directive 2011/83/EU do not apply, though a durable-medium confirmation is still due. Article 40: in force on the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal; applies from [12 months after the entry into force], bracketed in the proposal. Recitals 77 to 81 explain these rules. A proposal, not law; it names no agent protocol.

sources.title: Commission strengthens consumer protection laws, making them fit for the digital age (IP/26/2407)
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 through the press corner API (api/documents?reference=IP/26/2407&language=en, HTTP 200): eventDate 2026-11-11, publishDate 2026-11-11T11:14:11+01:00. The release says consumers will have clear rights when they use an AI agent to buy products on their behalf, and that the package includes a simplification directive and a consumer enforcement initiative.

sources.title: Legislative Observatory procedure file 2026/0356(COD): Digital Fairness Act
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200, after a redirect to oeil.europarl.europa.eu). Regulation repealing Directive 2005/29/EC; stage reached: Preparatory phase in Parliament; committee responsible and committee for opinion both pending a final decision on the referral; key event 2026-11-11, legislative proposal published (COM(2026)1100).

sources.title: The EU Digital Fairness Act Proposal: European Commission Proposes Major Update of EU Consumer Law
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (WebFetch). Law firm commentary dated 2026-11-18. It reads the automated-system obligations as falling primarily on the trader that makes the system available to consumers, and notes that Articles 26 and 27 do not address who bears liability when an automated system makes an error.

sources.title: EO 12866 regulatory review: rules under review (XML)
sources.publisher: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (Office of Management and Budget)
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200, 97,910 bytes; RUNDATE 2026-11-20). Three final rules received on 2026-11-18, each with a statutory deadline: RIN 3064-AG19, GENIUS Act Requirements for FDIC-Supervised Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers (FDIC); RIN 1506-AB73, Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer Anti-Money Laundering/Countering the Financing of Terrorism Program and Sanctions Compliance Program Requirements (FinCEN); and RIN 1506-AB72, Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Programs (FinCEN's general program rule, not an issuer rule). OIRA review comes before publication and the texts are not public. A different FDIC item, RIN 3064-ZA57 (proposed interagency guidance on commercial real estate concentrations), was received on 2026-11-16. The list is live, so later reads can differ.

sources.title: GENIUS Act Requirements and Standards for FDIC-Supervised Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers and Insured Depository Institutions (notice of proposed rulemaking, FR Doc. 2026-06974)
sources.notes: Federal Register API record read 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200): 91 FR 18534, RIN 3064-AG19, comments closed 2026-06-09. The FDIC's issuer proposal; OIRA lists the final rule under the same RIN as received on 2026-11-18 (src-policy-oira-eo12866-20261120).

sources.title: Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer Anti-Money Laundering/Countering the Financing of Terrorism Program and Sanctions Compliance Program Requirements (joint proposed rule, FR Doc. 2026-06963)
sources.publisher: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and Office of Foreign Assets Control (Federal Register)
sources.notes: Federal Register API record read 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200): joint proposed rule of FinCEN and OFAC, 91 FR 18582, RIN 1506-AB73, comments closed 2026-06-09. OIRA lists the final rule under the same RIN as received on 2026-11-18 (src-policy-oira-eo12866-20261120).

sources.title: Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions (proposed rule, FR Doc. 2026-23614)
sources.notes: Federal Register API record and full text read 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200): 91 FR 74514, RIN 1506-AB78, comments to 2027-01-19. Footnote 25 says permitted payment stablecoin issuers would also be covered by FinCEN's AML rules and cites the FinCEN and OFAC issuer proposal (91 FR 18582, 2026-04-10) and the joint FinCEN, OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC and NCUA issuer customer identification program proposal (91 FR 37234, 2026-06-22). A general customer due diligence proposal, not a GENIUS Act rule and not an agent rule.

sources.title: Federal Register API search: payment stablecoin, published since 2025-07-18
sources.notes: Run 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200): 44 documents, newest 2026-11-19. The only final rule from a primary federal payment stablecoin regulator is still the OCC's (FR Doc. 2026-21706, 91 FR 67000, 2026-10-23); Treasury's procedural interim final rule (FR Doc. 2026-19966, 91 FR 61688, 2026-09-30) invites comments to 2026-11-30. GENIUS Act proposals listed with their citations: Treasury, advance notice 2025-09-19 (90 FR 45159), state-regime principles 2026-04-03 (91 FR 16844) and issuance, offer and sale 2026-08-18 (91 FR 53368); FDIC, subsidiary approvals 2025-12-19 (90 FR 59409), issuer requirements 2026-04-10 (91 FR 18534) and BSA and sanctions standards 2026-06-05 (91 FR 34171); NCUA 2026-02-12 (91 FR 6531) and a supplemental proposal 2026-05-18 (91 FR 28956); FinCEN and OFAC issuer AML/CFT and sanctions programs 2026-04-10 (91 FR 18582); joint issuer customer identification program 2026-06-22 (91 FR 37234); OCC issuer AML/CFT and sanctions programs 2026-06-24 (91 FR 37840); Federal Reserve 2026-09-29 (91 FR 61580 and 91 FR 61346, comments to 2026-11-30). The public inspection list read the same day (issues of 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-25) held no GENIUS Act, FDIC or FinCEN rule.

sources.title: Some Potential Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (speech by Governor Michael S. Barr)
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200). Delivered 2026-11-16 at the Seventh Annual Association for Computing Machinery International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Finance, Milan. Barr says major banks now report finding AI agents attempting to take actions in retail customer accounts without the bank being able to verify authenticity, consent and alignment with customer instructions; he calls for strict authentication, explicit consent verification for specific actions, technical controls limiting agent capabilities and both rules- and values-based constraints, and says AI agents may accelerate deposit outflows during stress periods. He names no bank and gives no count. A speech, not guidance, a supervisory expectation or a rule.

sources.title: Considerations at the Intersection of Payments and Tokenized Markets (speech by Governor Christopher J. Waller)
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200). Delivered 2026-11-17 at The Clearing House Annual Conference 2026, New York. Waller says agentic commerce is still in the early stages and that tokenization and AI could be catalysts for one another; footnote 10 points to his Sibos 2026 speech, Payments in the Age of AI Agents, of 2026-09-29 (publication pub-waller-2026-sibos). A speech, not guidance.

sources.title: The courage to change (speech by Sarah Pritchard, deputy chief executive)
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200). First published and delivered 2026-11-19 at TheCityUK National Conference 2026, Bristol; the FCA notes it is a drafted speech that may differ from the delivered version. Pritchard says agentic products blur the line between regulated and unregulated activity, that a business describing itself as a technology provider cannot offer financial services without FCA authorization, and that firms developing or deploying personal agents should come to the FCA early to test their ideas. A speech, not guidance or a rule; it does not say that personal agents as such need authorization.

sources.title: FCA launches world-first platform giving firms new insight into AI innovation
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200; first published 2026-11-19). The FCA launched the AI Spotlight Observatory, developed with the Centre for Finance, Technology and Entrepreneurship (CFTE) and technology partner NayaOne: a resource of real-world AI use cases in financial services, from financial crime and compliance to emerging technologies such as agentic payments. A catalog of examples, not an assessment or endorsement of products.

sources.title: FCA publishes landmark review into impact of AI on retail financial services
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200; first published 2026-07-06). Announces AI and the future of retail financial services (The Mills Review), led by executive director Sheldon Mills and commissioned by the FCA Board. Its seven recommendations to the FCA Board and Executive include securing and adapting the regulatory perimeter, monitoring the transition to autonomous models and adapting regulatory frameworks, enabling the foundations for agentic finance and building an AI-enabled agentic supervisory model. A Yonder Consulting survey for the review (April 2026, more than 5,000 UK retail financial services consumers) found 20 percent likely to use AI capable of acting autonomously within pre-set goals, which the FCA equates to 11 million UK adults. Recommendations to the regulator, not rules. The report itself (fca.org.uk/publications/corporate-documents/mills-review) was not read.

sources.title: AI Adoption Plan: Financial Services
sources.publisher: HM Treasury (independent report by the financial services AI Champions)
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 through the GOV.UK content API (HTTP 200): document type independent report, first published 2026-07-14T16:11+01:00, publishing organization HM Treasury. Written by the government's financial services AI Champions, Harriet Rees (Starling Bank) and Dr Rohit Dhawan (Lloyds Banking Group); ten recommendations, including agentic payments. The page says the government welcomes the plan and accepts the recommendations for government; it does not say which recommendations those are.

sources.title: Financial Services AI Adoption Plan (HTML attachment)
sources.publisher: HM Treasury (independent report by the financial services AI Champions)
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 through the GOV.UK content API (HTTP 200). Recommendation 10, agentic payments readiness (priority High), asks that HM Treasury's upcoming consultation on modernising payment services regulation be used to establish a trust framework for agentic payments, with standards built on three pillars: legal and liability frameworks, Know Your Agent (KYA) protocols, and authentication and governance standards, led first by industry and possibly convened by the Centre for Finance, Innovation and Technology (CFIT). The Champions' recommendation, not government policy.

sources.title: The Final Missing Pieces of America's Stablecoin Rulebook Have Arrived at White House
sources.notes: Read 2026-11-21 (WebFetch). Byline Rebecca Montecinos, 2026-11-20 3:26 PM EST. Says the FDIC delivered its final stablecoin prudential rule to the White House on November 16 and FinCEN submitted its AML and sanctions compliance framework on November 18. The FDIC date conflicts with OIRA, which records 2026-11-18 for RIN 3064-AG19 (src-policy-oira-eo12866-20261120); the site follows OIRA. OIRA lists a different FDIC item, RIN 3064-ZA57, as received 2026-11-16; whether that explains the difference is not known.

events.title: GENIUS Act signed (Public Law 119-27)
events.detail: First US federal framework for payment stablecoins. It takes effect on the earlier of 2027-01-18 or 120 days after final implementing rules; the OCC's final rule of 2026-10-23 names 2027-01-18 as the effective date. It does not address AI agents as payers.

events.title: CFPB reopens the open banking rule (section 1033 reconsideration)
events.detail: The advance notice asks who may act as a consumer's representative, a question that will shape agent access to account data. It is not an agent rule.

events.title: Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act fully in force
events.detail: From this date payment service providers must have risk management and funds safeguarding frameworks under Bank of Canada supervision.

events.title: Visa's rules add requirements for agentic payments
events.detail: The 2025-10-18 edition of the Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules added the Visa Intelligent Commerce program to the rules (effective 2025-11-04 in Chile). The rules govern Visa and its member institutions and yield to applicable law. An Agentic Payment Provider must enroll in the program and register with Visa, and may not combine several agent purchases into one transaction. Within Visa's system, the cardholder is responsible for its actions in an Agentic Transaction as if the cardholder had initiated it. Visa calls none of these agent rules a liability shift.

events.title: Amazon sues Perplexity over the Comet shopping agent
events.detail: Amazon alleges computer fraud (CFAA) and California CDAFA violations and asks for a preliminary injunction against agent access to Amazon accounts.

events.title: EU reaches provisional agreement on PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation
events.detail: Political deal between Parliament and Council. The Council adopted its first-reading positions on 2026-10-29 (see that event); as of 2026-11-14 neither act was in the Official Journal. The Council texts have no agent-specific provisions.

events.title: US district court enjoins Perplexity's agent from Amazon accounts
events.detail: Judge Chesney grants Amazon a preliminary injunction with a seven-day administrative stay. The Ninth Circuit stays it on 2026-03-16 pending appeal. Exact dates come from press reports; the appellate opinion says March 2026.

events.title: FCA payments priorities name agentic AI payments
events.detail: The FCA says it will work with HM Treasury and consider whether payments regulation needs to change to support agentic AI payments.

events.title: Canada's Stablecoin Act receives Royal Assent in Bill C-15
events.detail: Part of the Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 (S.C. 2026, c. 3). The Act was not in force on 2026-10-19 and no commencement order had appeared by 2026-11-14; orders of the Governor in Council will set its commencement. Once in force, the Bank of Canada will supervise issuers. The proposed Stablecoin Regulations of 2026-10-24 say the government intends the framework to take effect in fall 2027.

events.title: Senator Warner asks Treasury about AI agents in finance
events.detail: Letter to Treasury Secretary Bessent asks Treasury to examine agentic payment rails and how existing law allocates liability when agents make errors or enable fraud.

events.title: MiCA transitional period for crypto-asset service providers ends
events.detail: Firms without MiCA authorization must stop serving EU clients and run their wind-down plans. Some member states ended the period earlier.

events.title: MAS publishes SAFR, a framework for governing AI agents in finance
events.detail: Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime is an information paper developed with industry under MAS's BuildFin.ai initiative. It sets out how agent actions are authorized, when human oversight steps in and what is recorded at each decision. A framework paper, not a rule.

events.title: FCA's Mills Review recommends building the foundations for agentic finance
events.detail: Led by executive director Sheldon Mills for the FCA Board, the review makes seven recommendations to the FCA, among them enabling the foundations for agentic finance and adapting regulatory frameworks as autonomous models spread. A survey for the review found 20 percent of UK consumers likely to use AI that acts autonomously within pre-set goals. Recommendations to the regulator, not rules.

events.title: HM Treasury consults on modernising payment services regulation
events.detail: The consultation (closed 2026-10-06) asks how authentication, consent and liability rules should adapt for agentic payments, alongside tokenized payments and Open Banking. The same day HM Treasury published an independent AI adoption plan whose Recommendation 10 asks that this consultation build a trust framework for agentic payments, including Know Your Agent protocols. No government response had been published by 2026-11-21.

events.title: EU Digital Omnibus on AI enters into force
events.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 moves Annex III high-risk obligations to 2027-12-02 and Annex I to 2028-08-02, and adds a grace period to 2026-12-02 for Article 50(2) marking by existing generative systems.

events.title: Worldpay: no liability shift yet for agent card payments
events.detail: Analysis from an acquirer: properly tokenized agent transactions follow existing rules, while liability for disputes short of fraud is unresolved.

events.title: EU AI Act general application date, including Article 50 transparency
events.detail: The general date of application of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, kept by the Digital Omnibus. Chatbot-style disclosure duties under Article 50 apply from here.

events.title: Ninth Circuit vacates the Amazon v. Perplexity injunction
events.detail: Published opinion: on this record the user, not Perplexity, accesses Amazon through the agent, so Amazon is unlikely to win its CFAA and CDAFA claims. Remanded; the court limited the ruling to its record.

events.title: EMVCo publishes a draft framework for card-based agentic payments
events.detail: Draft for comment until 2026-09-30, proposing Intent Services. EMVCo lists Know Your Agent and Agentic Transaction Indicators as possible future work.

events.title: Ant International, Mastercard and Visa start Know Your Agent interoperability work
events.detail: The three will explore common principles across their existing protocols (Visa TAP, Mastercard Verifiable Intent, Ant's Agentic Mobile Protocol), working through the MAS-convened BuildFin.ai platform and building on the SAFR framework. No network rule change announced.

events.title: Ninth Circuit denies Amazon's petition for rehearing en banc in Amazon v. Perplexity
events.detail: No judge asked for a vote. The mandate issued on 2026-09-18, so the 2026-08-04 judgment vacating the injunction took effect and the case continued in the district court.

events.title: Amazon amends its complaint against Perplexity with a claim based on its Agent Terms
events.detail: The First Amended Complaint keeps the CFAA and CDAFA counts and adds tortious interference with contractual relations, resting on the Agent Terms that Amazon added to its Conditions of Use on 2025-05-30. Those terms require an agent to identify itself, including in its user agent string, a self-declared label rather than a signed identity.

events.title: MAS issues Guidelines on AI Risk Management
events.detail: Effective 2027-10-07, with some expectations phased to 2028-10-07. MAS plans to consult on more agentic AI guidance in 2027.

events.title: Perplexity moves to dismiss Amazon's amended complaint
events.detail: The motion to dismiss and stay discovery was set for hearing on 2026-11-20 before Judge Chesney; trial is set for 2027-09-27. No ruling as of 2026-11-14.

events.title: EBA classifies USDC as the first significant e-money token under MiCA
events.detail: USDC, issued in the EU by Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS, is under the dual supervision MiCA sets for significant e-money tokens from 2026-11-12: the EBA directly supervises own funds, the reserve of assets, liquidity and recovery and redemption plans, and the French ACPR keeps governance and the other areas.

events.title: FCA says it will develop a trusted framework for agentic finance
events.detail: In a speech, the FCA's chief data, information and intelligence officer said the FCA will work with industry, other regulators and frontier labs on agent identity, delegated authority, accountability and execution. A companion page of AI good-practice examples says it creates no new requirements. No rule or consultation had followed by 2026-11-14.

events.title: OCC publishes the first primary-regulator final rule under the GENIUS Act
events.detail: Announced on 2026-10-21 and published as FR Doc. 2026-21706 (91 FR 67000), the rule covers payment stablecoin issuers under the OCC's jurisdiction and takes effect on 2027-01-18, together with the Act. The OCC calls it the first final rule from a primary federal payment stablecoin regulator; Treasury's procedural interim final rule on state certifications came earlier, on 2026-09-30. Bank Secrecy Act, AML and sanctions rules follow in a separate rulemaking. It has no provision on AI agents. No FDIC, Federal Reserve, NCUA or Treasury final rule implementing the Act had been published by 2026-11-21; the FDIC's rule reached White House review on 2026-11-18.

events.title: Canada prepublishes proposed Stablecoin Regulations
events.detail: Proposed, not final: issuer rules under the Stablecoin Act, and payment service providers that perform payment functions with stablecoins from listed issuers would come under the Retail Payment Activities Act. The government intends the rules to take effect in fall 2027, with the Act; comments were invited for 60 days.

events.title: Council adopts its first-reading positions on PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation
events.detail: Both files await the European Parliament's second reading (indicative plenary 2026-12-14) and are not yet in the Official Journal. Most PSR rules would apply 21 months after entry into force, when PSD3 must also apply. Neither text has an AI-agent provision; a PSR recital says strong customer authentication applies when a merchant-initiated mandate is set up, not to each later merchant-initiated payment.

events.title: UK regulators publish a joint statement on protecting people in an agentic economy
events.detail: The members of the Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum (CMA, FCA, ICO and Ofcom) set out their work on agentic AI and how existing law applies to agents, as described on the CMA's GOV.UK pages (the statement itself was not readable). The CMA's guidance says a business answers for what its AI agent does as it would for an employee. A statement, not a rule.

events.title: OCC examiner framework puts an autonomous customer-facing payment agent in its highest risk tier
events.detail: OCC Bulletin 2026-54 gives examiners a framework for banks' use of super intelligence, the federal term for AI since Executive Order 14434 (published 2026-10-02). A fully autonomous, customer-facing payment agent sits in Tier 1 (critical), and agentic-commerce systems outside the bank's control are treated as a channel risk. The framework says it sets no supervisory expectations for banks: it is guidance, not a rule.

events.title: EMVCo reports hundreds of comments on its draft agentic payments framework
events.detail: After its Board of Advisors meeting in Hanoi (2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14), EMVCo says hundreds of comments were submitted in the public review and that the Advisors' input will help guide how its Agentic Payments Task Force addresses them. The v1.0 draft is unchanged and no final version or date is announced; Know Your Agent capabilities and interoperable transaction indicators remain future priorities.

events.title: European Commission proposes the Digital Fairness Act, with consumer rules for agents that buy
events.detail: COM(2026) 1100 would replace the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive. A business that offers consumers an automated system that concludes contracts for them would have to ask the consumer at first use to choose whether to confirm every contract, only certain types of contract under criteria the consumer sets, including a maximum price and a time limit for that choice, or none, and to disclose any payment it receives for proposing a contract or any conflict of interest, after which the consumer must confirm that contract whatever the earlier choice. These agent rules do not apply to the provision of financial services. A proposal, not law: Parliament's file is at the preparatory stage, and the text would apply 12 months after entry into force.

events.title: Fed Governor Barr says banks see AI agents attempting actions in retail accounts without verifiable consent
events.detail: Barr said major banks report AI agents attempting actions in retail customer accounts that the bank cannot verify for authenticity, consent and fit with the customer's instructions, and called for strict authentication, consent checks for specific actions and technical limits on what agents can do. Governor Waller said on 2026-11-17 that agentic commerce is still in its early stages. Speeches, not guidance.

events.title: FDIC and FinCEN GENIUS Act final rules reach White House review
events.detail: The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA), part of the White House Office of Management and Budget, lists the FDIC's rule for the stablecoin issuers it supervises and the anti-money-laundering and sanctions program rule of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) for permitted payment stablecoin issuers (proposed with the Office of Foreign Assets Control on 2026-04-10) as received on 2026-11-18. Review comes before publication: neither text is public, and neither was in the Federal Register by 2026-11-21. The Act still takes effect on 2027-01-18.

events.title: Singapore names safe agentic transactions a national AI mission and plans an Agentic Money Sandbox
events.detail: Deputy Prime Minister and MAS Chairman Gan Kim Yong said agents must act within defined authority and limits, that institutions stay accountable for what agents do on their behalf, and that MAS will test with industry how agents can use purpose bound money. MAS and the Future of Finance Institute said the institute will establish a sandbox in which financial institutions test agent-initiated payments and treasury management with digital money. Statements of intent: no start date or rule is given.

events.title: MAS will facilitate the development of a know-your-agent protocol for customer agents
events.detail: In the new phase of SAFR (Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime), the protocol would let customer agents and financial institutions exchange who an agent is and whom it represents, its authority, its mandate and the assurance about its provenance, so that institutions can open a secure channel for agent access. Managing Director Chia Der Jiun also described the sandbox's payments case, where verified customer agents pay with tokenized deposits or stablecoins, and advised against giving personal agents financial logins. A plan: no specification, timeline or participants.

events.title: GENIUS Act and the OCC's implementing rule take effect (scheduled)
events.detail: Eighteen months after enactment. The OCC's final rule (published 2026-10-23) takes effect the same day and names it as the Act's effective date; final rules issued after about 2026-09-20 could not bring the date earlier, because 120 days would fall after 2027-01-18.
